en: The Apadāna of the Elder Potthakadāyaka The Chapter on the Golden Couch (Suvaṇṇabibbohanavagga), Number 6 [Verse 1] I gave a book to the Buddha, the Teacher, the Great Sage, who was seated upon a couch of gold. By that root of merit, I have attained the fruit of Stream-entry. May I never again fall into the states of woe. [2] [Verse 2] I gave a book to the Buddha, the Teacher, the Great Sage, who was seated upon a couch of gold. By that root of merit, I have attained the fruit of Once-returning. May I never again fall into the states of woe. [3] [Verse 3] I gave a book to the Buddha, the Teacher, the Great Sage, who was seated upon a couch of gold. By that root of merit, I have attained the fruit of Non-returning. May I never again fall into the states of woe. [4] [Verse 4] I gave a book to the Buddha, the Teacher, the Great Sage, who was seated upon a couch of gold. By that root of merit, I have attained the state of an Arhat. May I never again fall into the states of woe. [5] [Verse 5] I gave a book to the Buddha, the Teacher, the Great Sage, who was seated upon a couch of gold. By that root of merit, I have become a Wheel-turning Monarch. May I never again fall into the states of woe. [6] [Verse 6] I gave a book to the Buddha, the Teacher, the Great Sage, who was seated upon a couch of gold. By that root of merit, I have become a Sakka, Lord of the Gods. May I never again fall into the states of woe. [7] [Verse 7] I gave a book to the Buddha, the Teacher, the Great Sage, who was seated upon a couch of gold. By that root of merit, I have become a Māra, Lord of the World. May I never again fall into the states of woe. [31] [Verse 31] I gave a book to the Buddha, the Teacher, the Great Sage, who was seated upon a couch of gold. By that root of merit, I have become a Lord Without Rival. May I never again fall into the states of woe. [32] [Verse 3
“With reference to the Teacher, the Dhamma,
and the Saṅgha of the Great Seer,
this gift of a book was given by me.”
To those supreme ones worthy of offerings;
that deed which I performed back then, ninety-one eons ago—
I do not know a state of woe;
this is the fruit of giving cloth.
the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed did the venerable elder Potthakadāyaka speak these verses.
The legend of the Elder Potthakadāyaka is the sixth.
